home.title: Home
home.description: I write about problems I encounter while developing software and what I learn along the way.

blog.title: Posts
blog.description: Notes on software development and things I have learned.

about.title: About
about.description: Meet Jingeon Kim, a software engineer writing about the decisions behind building and running services and side projects.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: What visit statistics this blog collects and how to turn them off.

cognitive-surrender-side-project.title: The side project where I came close to cognitive surrender
cognitive-surrender-side-project.description: Addy Osmani's writing on cognitive surrender made me look back at leaving detailed conditions and design to an agent in my side projects. I cover the cases I filled in later, the disappointing screens, and why I stop at offloading at work.

reviewing-ai-output.title: The criteria I developed while reviewing AI-generated code and writing
reviewing-ai-output.description: In side projects, I delegated implementation, detailed tests, and AWS CLI and MCP setup. I tried the results, gave feedback, skimmed the code structure, and edited the writing and screens people would see.

side-project-design.title: Giving an AI agent autonomy, then reviewing and revising what it built
side-project-design.description: I delegated implementation and detailed tests for Pisik, Game Mate, and this blog, then tried the screens and skimmed their structure to give feedback on layouts, anonymous history, group permissions, and chat retries.

puppeteer-event-lifecycle.title: Waiting for Puppeteer requests and responses without leaking listeners
puppeteer-event-lifecycle.description: After reloading a page, an Electron collector had to wait until it had caught both a request's headers and a file's password. Fixing the code that polled a variable every second, I let a closure collect the values and a Promise end the wait and clean up the listeners.

electron-module-boundaries.title: Separating responsibilities in an Electron data-collection app
electron-module-boundaries.description: I set out to copy an existing file to add a recruiting site to an Electron app that collects applicant data, and stopped when I saw it would add another copy of the same post-login workflow. NestJS came in and left five days later, but the split between request handling, collection order, and site-specific processing stayed.

query-key-factory.title: Keeping TanStack Query keys and query functions together
query-key-factory.description: After editing an applicant's memo, I had to search for strings to find the cache to refresh. This is how I moved TanStack Query keys from enums and call-site arrays to Query Key Factory. It also puts custom functions and v5 queryOptions in one table, and separates what I chose then from what I would compare for a new build now.

typescript-patterns.title: Using TypeScript to catch mistakes at the call site
typescript-patterns.description: Each TypeScript pattern here, satisfies, optional properties, generics, and mutually exclusive props, sits beside the code you get without it. They catch mistakes that otherwise pass type checks, at the place the value is passed. Each entry stands alone, so you can read only the one you need.

nextjs-tanstack-query-ssr.title: Using TanStack Query with the Next.js App Router
nextjs-tanstack-query-ssr.description: I followed the code that lets the browser's TanStack Query cache pick up data fetched ahead of time in a Next.js Server Component. QueryClient gets a different lifetime in each environment, and both sides share the query definitions.

reservation-form-state.title: Moving reservation form state from Zustand to React Hook Form
reservation-form-state.description: Adding a family member to a hospital reservation form left date selection behaving as if the old participant count still applied. A server response cache, a global store, and component state each held their own copy of the same selections and dates. I separated the family list the server owns from the choices the user makes, and moved ongoing edits into React Hook Form alone.

review-like-optimistic-update.title: Updating review likes in list and detail caches
review-like-optimistic-update.description: The same hospital review appears in a list and on a detail screen, and liking it changed only the side where the button was pressed. I moved the like value into TanStack Query's cache, updated both before the response arrived, and restored saved snapshots when the request failed. This walks through that implementation in six steps with v5 code.

nextjs-seo-prefetch.title: When to await prefetch in the Next.js App Router
nextjs-seo-prefetch.description: The reservation detail page looked fine in the browser, yet the first HTML from the server lacked hospital information, and that HTML is also what a search crawler receives first. The server was starting its query without waiting for it. Starting prefetch did not mean the server was ready to pass its data along.

review-form-funnel.title: Separating state and steps in a review form
review-form-funnel.description: Moving a multi-step hospital review form from global stores to React Hook Form and Zod also meant reconnecting treatment selection. I changed the sheet to cancel on close and write selections to the form only after confirmation.

typed-program-form.title: Sharing a program form across two admin apps
typed-program-form.description: A program is a treatment product a hospital registers. Sharing its inputs across two admin apps, I widened what the code checks from field-name enums to value types to conversion tests. This post covers where Ant Design Form loses value types and how I separated what to share from what each app keeps.

cross-domain-token-handoff.title: Handing authentication between separate hosts
cross-domain-token-handoff.description: Moving a business admin app's settlement screen to another domain left the login cookies behind. To spare people a second login, I put tokens in a URL and then in a POST body, and each fix exposed the next hole. The authentication state duplicated across the two hosts is still unsolved.

chatbot-message-layer.title: Connecting two SSE streams to one chat interface
chatbot-message-layer.description: An AI support screen received AI answers and counselor messages over SSE from two different servers. SSE is a way for a server to keep an HTTP response open and send messages as they come. I connected the screen to the session stream only and kept the AI stream just to trigger generation. Giving up token-by-token display got me a screen that does not show the same answer twice, with no backend changes.

sitemap-api-boundaries.title: Separating public and authenticated reads in a sitemap
sitemap-api-boundaries.description: After I cached the generated sitemap, a shared Axios interceptor turned out to be reading authentication cookies even on public API calls that needed no login. A cached function can't use request-specific cookies, so I separated public reads from member-specific reads. Modification times and failure handling still have work left.

payment-coupon-branches.title: Handling coupon branches in payment history
payment-coupon-branches.description: Adding coupons to the payment history screen used by hospitals and operations made payment method alone insufficient to choose which details to show. Moving five if branches to ts-pattern's match kept the same decision order, so the next day I grouped rows by saved state first. Automated tests still do not cover combinations of method, status, and saved state.

fsd-layer-boundaries.title: Redrawing FSD boundaries for the codebase
fsd-layer-boundaries.description: The folders followed FSD, and I still could not explain where a new file should go. Dropping entities and regrouping domain code and screen composition, I found a counterexample to a new rule just over an hour later, hit a 633-second test run, and broke screens that had passed type checks.

prototype-working-rules.title: Keeping working rules from a prototype migration
prototype-working-rules.description: Moving a validation SPA to a Next.js service meant asking a coding agent to build similar features repeatedly, so I put recurring corrections into skills, the instruction documents the agent reads. Short, absolute rules could push it to change perfectly good code too, and I had to write down when each rule did not apply.

testing-standards.title: The standards I developed while introducing tests
testing-standards.description: Registration requests that passed on a fake server (a mock) returning 200 without inspecting the body were rejected by the real API. Failures like that kept adding to my standards for submission paths, mocks, and what assertions actually check. Here each rule sits next to what caused it, along with what stayed in CI.

declarative-code.title: How I write declarative code
declarative-code.description: Some components made me read query sequencing and calculations before I could see the screen. These cases, a review detail page, a settlement summary, search filters, and coupon calculations, show how I separated what a screen contains from how it gets made.

nextjs-server-client-issues.title: Tracing Next.js routing and cache problems
nextjs-server-client-issues.description: These are incidents from working with Next.js. Searches left the URL unchanged, an upgrade got JavaScript files blocked by CORS, and a deployment stopped notices from closing in old tabs. Form values disappeared when they should have stayed and stayed when they should have gone. Tracing the causes led me to sort out what the server has to handle again and what can finish in the browser.

error-boundary-recovery.title: Letting failed sections recover with Error Boundaries
error-boundary-recovery.description: One failed list query took the menu and header down with it. I decided what should remain on screen for each kind of failure, then moved where data is fetched and where Error Boundaries sit to match.

low-effort-success.title: Making the next success take less effort
low-effort-success.description: Asked to rank four experiences, split by success or failure and by effort or no effort, I put the effortful ones first. Afterward I wondered whether work completed with little effort should really rank lower, and my experience with coding agents gave me another way to read the question.

sentry-observability.title: Defining Sentry collection policies and verifying delivery and source maps
sentry-observability.description: I limited sensitive collection and prioritized errors by user impact, then checked SDK behavior, Web Vitals delivery and storage, MCP access, and source-map artifacts in our benefits portal.

plan-gated-ai-workflow.title: The development workflow I refined with coding agents
plan-gated-ai-workflow.description: A coding agent reported a passing E2E that was waiting for text found nowhere in the repository to disappear. This is how I delegate implementation while still reading the pre-implementation plan and the finished diff myself, in order from ticket to deployment, with what actually caught me at each step.

zod-assertion-boundaries.title: Runtime validation beyond type assertions
zod-assertion-boundaries.description: TypeScript's as checks nothing at runtime, so it cannot stop a server from sending an unexpected value. Removing these assertions showed me that some places were better left without Zod. Where a schema did belong, I looked at who gets stuck when the value is wrong, and API responses, URLs, and forms ended up failing differently.

bottom-sheet-drag-crash.title: Tracing a Bottom Sheet drag crash with Sentry
bottom-sheet-drag-crash.description: A bottom sheet froze the screen when users released a drag. I traced the stack into the library's source and found the line reading null, but never reproduced the app action behind it, so I upgraded to a major version without that line. A conversion in the shared component kept snap positions in place, and I still missed a title that scrolled away with the body.

health-check-program.title: Bringing health-check reservations into the existing service
health-check-program.description: I brought health checks from phone inquiries into selection and payment inside a benefits portal, where users who arrive through partner companies find and book hospital programs. This follows the screens in order, from registration to returning from the payment window, including behavior that changed after I rechecked the first request.

reading-ai-code.title: Why I still read the code
reading-ai-code.description: A sprint I considered finished after checking screens led to many hotfixes. I now read code to find paths to test, then check those paths and the actual UI separately.

side-project-infrastructure.title: Starting with one EC2 instance
side-project-infrastructure.description: Balancing value for money, availability, and maintenance: agent-configured EC2 for two services, Vercel for the blog, and the tradeoffs of Lightsail, Lambda, and Workers.

side-project-technology.title: Choosing the stack and refining the structure of two side projects
side-project-technology.description: Why I chose the APIs, caches, database safeguards, and observability tools for two side projects, and how I set the direction while delegating implementation and detailed verification to an agent.

design-concepts-for-reading-ui.title: Design concepts that explain why an interface feels awkward
design-concepts-for-reading-ui.description: Coaching cards make design concepts concrete: what to read first, what looks related, how to act, and how to recover when something fails.
